title: Reviews and reports
hired_for: To know the state of the business in 5 minutes a week and show it to a partner or client without building slides; agencies hire it to see every client on one page.

jobs.job: Tell me in 5 minutes what happened this week and what needs my call
jobs.why: The owner cannot read 6 dashboards every Monday. Without one short page, a problem sits for weeks because nobody put it in front of the person who decides.

watch.metric: decisions logged from the weekly review, per week
watch.source: brand brain (decision log)

drives.metric: days from a number crossing its line to a decision

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the founder spends 90 minutes across Shopify, Meta and Klaviyo and logs 0 decisions. After: 5 minutes, 1 page, 3 decisions logged.

jobs.job: Show profit after ads each week, not just sales
jobs.why: Sales can rise while the business loses money on every order. The owner wants the profit left after product cost, shipping, discounts and ad spend, every week.

watch.metric: profit after product cost, shipping, discounts and ad spend, weekly
watch.source: Shopify orders with product cost, Meta and Google Ads spend

drives.metric: gross profit

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the weekly note says sales up 12%. After: it also says profit after ads fell from $18,400 to $15,900, driven by a deeper discount.
jobs.who_today: founder or bookkeeper, monthly and late

jobs.job: Send the client or partner a monthly report without building slides
jobs.why: Agencies and founders lose a day a month copying numbers into slides. The report should be ready when the month closes, with the same numbers the team uses.

watch.metric: days from month end to report sent
watch.source: brand brain (report log)

drives.metric: client retention, agency accounts kept per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the report goes out on the 9th after 6 hours of copying. After: it goes out on the 2nd, checked in 20 minutes.

jobs.job: Catch a number that has been off for 2 weeks before it becomes a month
jobs.why: One bad week is noise. Two in a row is a trend. The owner wants a flag when a key number sits outside its normal range 2 weeks running.

watch.metric: key numbers outside their normal range for 2 or more weeks
watch.source: Shopify, GA4, Meta, Klaviyo via the metric contract

drives.metric: gross profit lost to drops found late

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 20% drop in email revenue went unseen for 5 weeks. After: it is flagged in week 2 with the flow that broke.

jobs.job: See every client on one page and find who is in trouble
jobs.why: An agency with 15 brands checks them tab by tab and finds problems late. The owner wants one page that ranks clients by what needs attention.

watch.metric: clients with a key number outside its normal range for 2 or more weeks
watch.source: each brand's metric contract (Shopify, Meta, Google Ads)

drives.metric: client churn, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the agency learns a client is unhappy from the client. After: 3 of 15 clients are flagged on Monday, each with the number that slipped.

jobs.job: Check the agency's or ad platform's report against our own numbers
jobs.why: Ad platforms and agencies count their own credit. The owner wants the store's real orders set next to what was claimed, before moving money on it.

watch.metric: gap between orders the platform claims and store orders from that channel, same window
watch.source: Meta and Google Ads reporting, Shopify orders, GA4

drives.metric: ad spend moved on overstated credit

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Meta reports 410 purchases, the agency report shows 410. After: the page shows 410 claimed against 265 store orders tagged to Meta, and notes a 7-day versus 1-day window mismatch.

jobs.job: Show where growth came from: new customers or returning ones
jobs.why: Total sales hide whether the business is finding new buyers or leaning on old ones. Each needs a different fix.

watch.metric: new-customer orders and returning-customer orders, weekly
watch.source: Shopify orders

drives.metric: gross profit from new versus returning customers

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: orders up 8%. After: new-customer orders down 11%, returning up 24%, so paid ads need a look.

jobs.job: Show sales after returns and chargebacks next to sales booked
jobs.why: Booked sales that come back as returns or disputes are not sales. The owner wants both lines, so growth is real.

watch.metric: sales after returns, refunds and chargebacks, weekly
watch.source: Shopify orders, refunds and disputes

drives.metric: gross profit

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $212,000 booked in September. After: $212,000 booked, $183,000 kept after returns and disputes, return rate up 3 points.

jobs.job: Show customer health next to the money: reviews, tickets and reply time
jobs.why: Sales can hold for a month while service falls apart. The owner wants review rating and support backlog on the same page as profit.

watch.metric: first reply time in hours and open ticket backlog, weekly; review rating, 30 days
watch.source: Gorgias, review app

drives.metric: repeat purchase rate, 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: support is checked only when a customer complains. After: first reply time of 31 hours shows up next to profit, and a second person is added.

jobs.job: Know early if this quarter's goals are on track
jobs.why: Finding out at quarter end is too late to act. The owner wants each goal shown against the pace needed, every week.

watch.metric: progress on each quarterly goal versus the pace needed to hit it
watch.source: brand brain (goals), metric contract

drives.metric: quarter gross profit versus plan

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the repeat rate goal is checked in the last week of the quarter. After: in week 5 it shows 41% of target with 8 weeks left, on pace to miss.

jobs.job: Explain why a number moved, not just that it moved
jobs.why: A line going down tells the owner to worry, not what to do. The report should name the cause: price, stock, an ad, a site change or the season.

watch.metric: share of top movers each week with a named cause
watch.source: metric contract with Shopify, GA4, Meta, brand brain change log

drives.metric: days from a number moving to a decision

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'Conversion down 14%'. After: 'Conversion down 14%, mostly from the best seller in size M going out of stock on the 12th'.

jobs.job: Decide next month's channel budget split from one view
jobs.why: Each channel owner asks for more. The owner wants one view of where the next dollar earns the most, and a flag when spend drifts from what was agreed.

watch.metric: each channel's share of spend versus the agreed split
watch.source: Meta, Google Ads, Klaviyo costs, brand brain (agreed split)

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Meta has drifted to 71% of spend against 60% agreed. After: the split is reset and cost per new customer drops from $48 to $42 in a month.

jobs.job: Show what our tests and changes earned this month
jobs.why: A report that lists numbers but not the work behind them cannot show if the team is worth it. The owner wants each month tied to the changes that moved it.

watch.metric: gross profit banked from changes rolled out this month
watch.source: brand brain (experiment registry), Shopify

drives.metric: gross profit growth, month over month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the report shows results with no link to work done. After: 3 changes rolled out, $6,200 a month in profit banked, shown next to the totals.

jobs.job: Flag when stock and ad spend are out of step
jobs.why: Spending on ads for a product about to run out wastes money. Holding back ads on overstocked items ties up cash. The weekly page should show both.

watch.metric: days of stock left on the top 10 sellers next to their ad spend, weekly
watch.source: Shopify inventory, Meta and Google Ads spend by product

drives.metric: sales lost to stockouts

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,100 a week is spent on an item with 6 days of stock. After: spend moves to an item with 90 days of stock.

jobs.job: Report money in, profit and cash as 3 separate numbers
jobs.why: A profitable month can still leave the bank empty if stock was bought. The owner wants sales, profit and cash side by side, never blended into one story.

watch.metric: cash on hand at week end versus the lowest point in the 13-week forecast
watch.source: brand brain (cash entered weekly from the bank; proxy until a bank feed connects)

drives.metric: weeks of cash left

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the month shows $22,000 profit and the owner is surprised by a tight bank balance. After: the report shows profit $22,000, stock bought $31,000, cash down $9,000.

jobs.job: Make every number come from one agreed source
jobs.why: When Shopify, GA4 and the agency each give a different sales number, meetings turn into arguments. The owner wants one source per number, written down.

watch.metric: report fields with a missing or conflicting source
watch.source: metric contract; GA4 purchases versus Shopify orders for the same dates

drives.metric: decisions made on the wrong number

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: GA4 shows 18% fewer purchases than Shopify and 2 reports use each. After: every field names its source, and the gap is shown as its own line.

jobs.job: Check a vendor invoice against what was actually delivered
jobs.why: Agencies and freelancers bill for work that was late, partial or never done. The owner wants each invoice line matched to delivered work before paying.

watch.metric: invoice dollars with no matching delivered work, per month
watch.source: brand brain (vendor invoices and delivered work log)

drives.metric: vendor spend per piece of work delivered

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $2,400 a month is paid for 8 ad creatives; 5 arrived. After: the gap is flagged before payment and the invoice is cut to match.

jobs.job: Compare this month with the same month last year, fairly
jobs.why: A sale that fell on different dates, or a holiday shift, makes a normal month look like a crisis or a boom. The owner wants year on year with the calendar noted.

watch.metric: sales and gross profit, this month versus the same month last year, with sale and holiday dates marked
watch.source: Shopify orders, brand brain (marketing calendar)

drives.metric: forecast accuracy for the next month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: October looks 22% down on last year. After: last year's sale fell in October, this year's in September; like for like is 3% up.

jobs.job: Show which products make money and which only make sales
jobs.why: A best seller can lose money after discounts, shipping and returns. The monthly report should rank products by profit, not by sales alone, so ads and stock follow profit.

watch.metric: gross profit per product after discounts and returns, monthly
watch.source: Shopify orders, refunds and product cost

drives.metric: gross margin

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the report lists the top 10 products by sales. After: it ranks them by profit; the number 2 seller earns $1.10 per order after returns and its ad budget is cut.

jobs.job: Track actual against budget and forecast every month
jobs.why: Without a monthly check, spend creeps up and targets slip quietly. The owner wants the gap to plan named, with the action that closes it.

watch.metric: sales and profit after ads versus budget, monthly
watch.source: Shopify, ad platforms, brand brain (budget)

drives.metric: cash at quarter end versus plan

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the budget lives in a spreadsheet nobody opens. After: September shows profit after ads 9% under budget, with the 2 lines that caused it.

jobs.job: Draft the board or investor update from real numbers
jobs.why: Investor updates take days and often use different numbers than the team does. The owner wants a first draft from the quarter's real figures and test results.

watch.metric: days from quarter end to update sent
watch.source: brand brain (report log)

drives.metric: investor follow-up questions about the numbers, per update

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the update goes out 4 weeks after quarter end. After: a draft is ready on day 3 and sent on day 7.

jobs.job: Catch an agency or freelancer delivering less than agreed, month after month
jobs.why: One short month can be an accident. Three in a row is a pattern. The owner wants delivered work checked against the contract over time.

watch.metric: delivered work versus committed amount in the contract, per period
watch.source: brand brain (contract terms and delivered work log)

drives.metric: vendor spend per piece of work delivered

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a contract promises 4 emails a month; 2 have gone out for 3 months. After: the pattern is flagged and the fee is renegotiated.

jobs.job: See if anyone on the team or agency is overloaded across brands
jobs.why: An overbooked account manager drops things, and clients leave. The agency owner wants booked hours per person across every brand, each week.

watch.metric: people booked over 100% of their available hours this week
watch.source: brand brain (team hours and task queues)

drives.metric: missed deliverables per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: an account manager runs 6 brands at 140% of hours. After: 2 brands move to a colleague and nobody is over 100%.

jobs.job: Cut the reports and meetings nobody uses
jobs.why: Every extra report and standing meeting takes hours from real work. The owner wants to see which ones are not read or do not lead to decisions.

watch.metric: recurring reports not opened in 30 days, and founder hours in standing meetings per week
watch.source: brand brain (report log and meeting calendar)

drives.metric: founder hours freed per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 7 recurring reports, 3 never opened, 9 hours of meetings a week. After: 4 reports, 5 hours, same decisions made.

jobs.job: Share a report with the right people and nobody else
jobs.why: A report sent to a partner or client can carry numbers for other brands or private costs. The owner wants each report to show only what that reader should see.

watch.metric: shared reports with access outside the named readers
watch.source: brand brain (share log)

drives.metric: private data exposed to the wrong reader

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the monthly deck is a shared link anyone can open. After: each report is tied to named readers, and 0 links are open to all.
